rationale: The traced clean-miss construction now shows the resend Decide being rejected as a sequence break and repaired: node 5 read `decide7:2-2>2-2|prepare:2-2>2-2|accsync1:2-2>3-3`, ending at accepted 3 and decided 3. That withdraws the strong 'no enabled repair' claim for a straight AcceptStopSign loss: when the leader's resend is ahead of the follower's expected sequence, the follower reconnects and the AcceptSync repairs it. The run-13 stall therefore needs a different explanation, so this experiment leaves the randomized seeded run unchanged and instead records what actually reaches and leaves the lagging node 3 during the 150 fair-delivery rounds, which the earlier receipt only summarized as an unchanged accepted index.

scope.description: Same five-node lossy stress with seed 0xbe5466cf34e90c6c, reconfigure at action 450 and 20 percent loss, run id 13; the 150-round convergence loop stops only when all decided indices agree. During convergence every queued message addressed to node 3 is delivered one at a time and up to twelve Paxos messages are recorded as kind+sequence counter with node 3's accepted and decided pair before and after, while PrepareReq and Promise messages sent by node 3 are counted.
assumptions: Ticking every node each round drives elections and resend timers; 150 rounds exceed the default 100-tick resend timeout.
Node 3 is the lagging follower identified by the earlier runs of this same seeded schedule.
Delivering node 3's messages one at a time changes only the order among messages already delivered in the same round, not which messages are delivered.
excluded: Starting the next configuration, snapshots, flexible quorums, crash-restart and Byzantine participants.

experiment.prefix: Identical to randomized_reconfig_diagnose_lag with run id 13, including the 900-action seeded schedule, the reconfigure at action 450, the 150-round convergence loop, all previous safety fields and the node-3 accepted/decided/leader/promise diagnostics. New in this revision: within each convergence round the harness first counts PrepareReq and Promise messages sent by node 3, then calls route_traced, which delivers the queued messages addressed to node 3 one at a time (recording at most twelve as kind+sequence counter and node 3's accepted-decided pair before and after) before routing the remaining messages; the same counting and traced delivery is repeated after the tick phase, and the joined trace plus both send counts are added to the safety event.

comparisons.description: Bounded convergence past the resend timeout: all nodes report the same decided index.

experiment.revision_reason: Keeps the seeded 900-action lossy run, reconfigure at action 450, 150-round fair-delivery convergence and every existing field unchanged, and adds a bounded ordered trace of the Paxos messages delivered to node 3 (kind, sequence counter, accepted/decided before and after) plus counts of PrepareReq and Promise messages node 3 sent during convergence.
